mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 2.5% over two consecutive quarters signals a tightening cycle that raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods when FEDFUNDS exceeds 2.5% for two consecutive quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate below 4% for three consecutive months indicates a tight labor market that pushes wage growth and input costs higher, compressing corporate margins and resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE is below 4% for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) of more than 2% signals weakening household demand, which reduces revenue expectations for consumer-facing firms and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 falls by more than 2% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months signals contraction in manufacturing activity, which reduces earnings for industrial firms and drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -0.5% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during three consecutive months of INDPRO declines exceeding -0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in FEDFUNDS and a fall in CPIAUCSL of more than 0.3 percentage points over two months signals a successful disinflationary tightening, which initially depresses growth but ultimately supports equity valuations via lower inflation risk, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises and CPIAUCSL falls by >0.3pp over two months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when FEDFUNDS rises and CPIAUCSL falls by more than 0.3pp over two months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Housing Starts Index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average by more than 10% for two consecutive months signals a housing market recovery that boosts construction-related equities and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 12-month moving average by >10% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during two consecutive months when HOUST exceeds its 12-month moving average by more than 10%.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in PAYEMS of more than 0.4% month-over-month and a fall in UNRATE below 3.5% for two consecutive months signals a strong labor market expansion that boosts consumer spending and corporate profits, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > +0.4% MoM and UNRATE < 3.5% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when PAYEMS rises by more than 0.4% MoM and UNRATE falls below 3.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent annual decline in Real Personal Savings (RSAFS) of more than 5% for three consecutive years signals reduced household savings and higher consumption financed by debt, which initially supports consumer discretionary stocks but ultimately increases default risk and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS annual change < -5% for three consecutive years
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when RSAFS declines by more than 5% annually for three consecutive years.
